clue.text: Tree competitor polled

indicators.note: a polled animal has had its head or horns taken off, so the first letter of the word goes

parts.note: a racer is someone competing in a race

explanation.surface: A tree is entered in some contest after being pollarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polled' means beheaded, removing the R from the front of RACER.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the botanical genus of maples, a familiar tree.

clue.text: Book fair, fair!

parts.note: right in the sense of just or fair-minded

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising a book fair.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'fair' means just; the second, with its exclamation mark, is the weather sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair weather is sunny and clear, which is synonymous with a bright day.

clue.text: Bone found in tart as stirred into dinner, say?

indicators.note: the stirred letters are placed into the middle of the meal word

parts.note: dinner is one example of a meal

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bone turns up in a tart mixed into someone's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirred' rearranges the clue's own letters; 'into' places the result inside the meal, which 'say?' marks as only one example of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A metatarsal is one of the long bones of the foot.

clue.text: Take over a century to separate foursome following the leader of government

indicators.note: the two letters split the four-letter run apart by sitting between its third and fourth letters

parts.words: foursome following the leader of government
parts.note: the leader of government is G; the four letters after it in the alphabet are H, I, J, K
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A political instruction about seizing power over a hundred years to split a quartet behind the head of government.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'foursome' is alphabetical: the four letters after G. A and C go between J and K.
explanation.definitionFit: To hijack something is to seize control of it by force, taking it over.

clue.text: Cupid after lips of some looker

indicators.note: Cupid's word comes after the edge letters
lips are the edges of something, so the outer letters of the word are taken

parts.note: Cupid is pictured as an archer with bow and arrows

explanation.surface: Cupid chasing after the lips of some good-looking person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lips of' gives the outer letters S and E of 'some'.
explanation.definitionFit: A searcher is one who looks for something, so a looker in the sense of seeker.

clue.text: See 25
See 23
Cosmetic: measure of volume impressing wrinkly a lot

indicators.note: to impress is to press into, so the cubic-centimetre letters hold the other word inside

parts.note: cc is cubic centimetres, a unit of volume
wrinkly is slang for an old person, so old
reams of something means a great quantity

explanation.surface: A beauty product whose dose pushes heavily into wrinkles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impressing' means pressing into, so the volume abbreviation holds the elderly word; 'Cosmetic' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold cream is an emollient face cream used for cleansing and softening skin.

clue.text: Brother smothering body part in 8 28

indicators.note: to smother is to cover over completely, so these letters surround the body part

parts.note: the answer to 8 is the word for chilly, abbreviated to its usual letter C
the answer to 28 in its sense of the best part, the elite
an arm is part of the body

explanation.surface: A friar buries his arm in face cream.
explanation.walkthrough: '8 28' is read as two pieces: cold gives C, cream (the best) gives ELITE, and together they smother ARM.
explanation.definitionFit: A Carmelite is a friar of the Carmelite order, addressed as Brother.

clue.text: Little publicity for doctor

parts.note: pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons
MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor gets only modest publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: A promo is a short promotional piece, an advertisement in miniature.

clue.text: Jamaican music, pattern of notes around ghetto originally

indicators.note: the melodic word goes around the single letter

parts.note: a raga is a melodic framework in Indian music

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Jamaican music described as a pattern of notes from the ghetto.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragga is a dancehall style of reggae from Jamaica using digital backing.

clue.text: Bloomer on radar, so wrong

indicators.note: the letters are put wrong, in a new order

explanation.surface: A blunder spotted on radar, so something is amiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, but it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron's rod is a tall plant, the great mullein, which flowers in summer.

clue.text: Work out second Beatles number

parts.note: to get something is to understand or figure it out
to second a motion is to back it

explanation.surface: Instructions to figure out another Beatles song.
explanation.definitionFit: Get Back was a Beatles single released in 1969.

clue.text: Mouth commercial rot

parts.note: gob is slang for mouth
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: Complaining that a spoken advertisement is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rot' looks like nonsense, but is the verb meaning decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that goes bad decays or spoils, so the phrase means to decay.

clue.text: Nothing revolutionary in the Butcher of the Somme coming down hard

indicators.note: the turned word goes in the general's surname

parts.note: Field Marshal Douglas Haig, commander at the Somme, earned the nickname for its huge casualties

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: nil means nothing, a score of zero

explanation.surface: A general's bloody reputation, with nothing revolutionary about it, comes crashing down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns the zero word round, and 'in' sets it within the general's name. 'coming down hard' is weather, not a fall from grace.
explanation.definitionFit: Hail is ice falling from the sky, and it lands hard, so it is precipitation pelting down.

clue.text: Top foreign figure is not surprisingly being discussed

indicators.note: topping something removes its head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: cinque is Italian for five

indicators.note: a surprising change signals the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A leading overseas personality is, unsurprisingly, the subject of debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' removes C from CINQUE leaving INQUE; 'surprisingly' rearranges IS NOT into STION.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter in question is one under debate or consideration.

clue.text: Imagine pub's out of stout

indicators.note: the pub word is taken out of the stout word

parts.note: Guinness is the best-known Irish stout
an inn is a pub; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Picture a bar that has run out of dark beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pub's out of stout' reads as 'pub is out of stout': INN removed from GUINNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To guess is to suppose or speculate without knowing, close to imagining.

clue.text: Flipping mug is our leader

indicators.note: flipping over turns the word backwards

parts.note: to mug someone is to rob them

explanation.surface: A grumble that a flipping idiot is in charge of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British expletive, but reverses ROB.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Johnson was the UK Prime Minister when this puzzle appeared, the nation's leader.

clue.text: Rifle unloaded, safe to carry a gun

indicators.note: unloading empties it, leaving only the outer letters
the safe word carries the letter A within it

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: A rifle without ammunition, kept safe, but someone wants to carry a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifle' looks like the definition but is emptied to RE. PETER holding A gives PEATER. Peter = safe is underworld slang (safe-crackers were peter men).
explanation.definitionFit: A repeater is a firearm that fires several shots without reloading.

clue.text: From a long way out, service returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A tennis serve hit back from a great distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like tennis but is the armed service.
explanation.definitionFit: Far means at a great distance, a long way away.

clue.text: Noted window cleaner almost catching priest's member

indicators.note: catching means holding on to, so the shortened name holds the priest
almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: George Formby, British comic entertainer, sang 'When I'm Cleaning Windows'
Eli is the priest in the Bible who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A famous window cleaner nearly grabs a clergyman's limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the entertainer's last letter; 'catching' sets the biblical priest inside. 'member' means a limb, not someone in a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A forelimb is a front leg or arm, a member of the body.

clue.text: File letter for audition?

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so this is how the letter sounds when spoken

parts.note: the letter in question is Q

explanation.surface: Lining up a letter to be considered for an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' looks like a tryout, but means hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A file is a line of people one behind another, as in single file.

clue.text: Premier League initially probing drugs cheat — some effect

indicators.note: something probing pushes inside, so the initials sit inside the cheat

parts.note: a doper is an athlete who takes drugs

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of these words

explanation.surface: Premier League investigations into a drugs cheat have an impact.
explanation.definitionFit: The Doppler effect is the change in frequency of a wave from a moving source.

clue.text: Lights out not later than beginning of evening — black, of course

parts.note: by means no later than, as in by five

indicators.note: beginning of means the word's first letter

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black on pencils
yes as an agreeing reply

explanation.surface: Bedtime by early evening, when it gets dark, naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Bye-byes is a nursery word for sleep or going to bed, when the lights go out.

clue.text: Fresh-faced youth is not out after bowled over

indicators.note: the altered word comes after the cricket letters

parts.note: B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: 'is not out' means the clue's 'is' takes the place of 'out'

explanation.surface: Cricket: a young batsman is out, bowled; he is not out after all.
explanation.walkthrough: In YOUTH, OUT is replaced by IS, giving YISH, after B and O (both cricket scorebook abbreviations).
explanation.definitionFit: Boyish looks are youthful, smooth and unlined.

clue.text: Absolutely what happens in Russian roulette?

definitions.meaning: an emphatic phrase of agreement, certainly
in Russian roulette a player literally wagers survival on a single pull of the trigger

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic yes, and taken literally describes staking existence on a gamble.

clue.text: Bug in 8 28, once whipped?

indicators.note: the insect goes inside the chilly word

parts.note: the answer to 8, cold, means chilly
an ant is an insect, loosely a bug

explanation.surface: An insect lands in cold cream, which is then whipped.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference splits: '8' alone supplies a synonym for cold, while '28' heads the definition, cream once whipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Chantilly is sweetened whipped cream, so cream once it has been whipped.

clue.text: Fifty having flown, see bird

indicators.note: something that has flown has left, so the letter is removed

parts.note: clock is slang for notice or see
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty having flown off, look at the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A cock is a male bird, especially a rooster.

clue.text: Period I spent in the morning, initially wasted

indicators.note: wasted means ruined, so the letters are broken up and reformed

parts.note: a.m. is short for ante meridiem, in the morning; initially points to the abbreviation

explanation.surface: A spell I spent in the morning, wasted at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' rearranges I SPENT with AM.
explanation.definitionFit: A timespan is a length of time, a period.

clue.text: Smalls shown by not entirely loyal supporter

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces sit side by side
not entirely means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: true means loyal, as in true friends
S is small, so two smalls are SS

explanation.surface: Underwear revealed by a supporter who is not entirely loyal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smalls' looks like British slang for underwear, but is two S's, placed after TRU.
explanation.definitionFit: A truss is a supporting belt for a hernia, or a supporting framework.

clue.text: Not all there, Johnson glibly lied

indicators.note: Not all there says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A politician, not fully with it, told glib lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lied' looks like the past of lie, but is the German word for an art song.
explanation.definitionFit: A lied is a German art song, as by Schubert.

clue.text: See 8
Is leading Tory in Mr Johnson ultimately to fail in his duty?

indicators.note: the pair go in the title Mr

parts.note: Michael Gove was a leading Conservative minister

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter

explanation.surface: Is a senior Conservative in Boris Johnson's cabinet set to let the country down?
explanation.walkthrough: IS and GOVE go 'in' MR, then the N that ends Johnson.
explanation.definitionFit: To misgovern is to rule badly, a leader neglecting proper duties.
